findings.explanation: getOrganizationWebhooksLogs returns only a log of webhook POSTs sent: alertType (human label), url, responseCode, responseDuration, sentAt, loggedAt, networkId and organizationId. It has no alertTypeId, device name or alert payload. It also only has entries once a webhook receiver is already configured, so it is neither an alternative nor simpler, and it cannot attribute motion events to a camera.
findings.quote: (2) `cisco_meraki_webhook_logs` polled input (sourcetype `meraki:webhooklogs:api`) — simpler to set up but capped to the Meraki webhook-logs retention window. This SPL queries both.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `meraki:webhook` (the HEC receiver) the only source of motion events. Describe `meraki:webhooklogs:api` as an optional delivery-health check (response codes, failed POSTs). Make the same correction in dataSources and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: dataSources says 'Camera motion alerts' and implementation says 'Motion alert'. Meraki labels this alert 'Motion detected' (alertTypeId motion_alert).
findings.quote: Subscribe to `Camera motion alerts` in the alert profile.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the Meraki names consistently: enable 'Motion detected' alerts (alertTypeId motion_alert) for the cameras, and add the Splunk webhook as a recipient under Network-wide > Alerts.

findings.explanation: The add-on has a 'Cameras' input (sourcetype meraki:cameras, getNetworkEvents with camera product type). It is unverified whether camera motion events appear in the network event log, so the absolute claim may be wrong.
findings.quote: they are NOT in the polled device-API surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether meraki:cameras events include motion-related event types. If they do, list them as a polled fallback; if not, keep the claim but name the meraki:cameras input as checked.

findings.explanation: The Meraki add-on is Splunkbase 5580 (Splunk_TA_cisco_meraki). splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5631 returns 404 and is not in the cached catalogue.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 5631 reference. Retitle the 5580 entry 'Cisco Meraki Add-on for Splunk'.

findings.explanation: A generic Cisco Security support index adds nothing for Meraki MV motion webhooks.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the Meraki webhook sample-alerts page and the add-on's webhook setup section instead.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `alertType="motionAlert"` never matches: Meraki sends alertType "Motion detected" with alertTypeId "motion_alert" (https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/webhooks/webhook-sample-alerts/). Only the alertTypeId branch works, and only for meraki:webhook. meraki:webhooklogs:api events carry neither alertTypeId nor deviceName, so that sourcetype adds nothing or NULL device rows. Filter on alertTypeId="motion_alert" in meraki:webhook and use the top-level deviceName.

summary: The webhook-based approach is sound. However, the text presents the polled webhook-logs input as an equivalent source of motion events, but that input only records delivery metadata. The SPL also filters on an alertType value Meraki never emits.
